title.narrative: Rapid Multi-Purpose Cash and Protection Response for Newly Displaced Families in Aleppo

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project, under Envelope 3 of the 2025 First Standard Allocation, outlines IYD's flexible and rapid response mechanism to address unforeseen critical needs arising from new displacements or sudden returns in Northwest Syria. Leveraging its established operational capacity and extensive experience in the region, IYD will provide immediate life-saving assistance and protection to affected populations within 48 hours of a crisis onset. The intervention will primarily focus on critical sectors such as Multi-Purpose Cash, Protection and Emergency Shelter and NFI, utilizing both in-kind and cash modalities. The project design is generic at this stage, with specific deployment plans, activities, and locations to be finalized upon the activation of an emergency response and in close coordination with OCHA and relevant stakeholders. IYD's approach prioritizes the safety, dignity, and resilience of conflict-affected communities, ensuring gender-sensitive and inclusive programming, robust accountability mechanisms, and seamless integration with existing humanitarian efforts.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtIYD is a SCHF-eligible national NGO with extensive experience implementing multi-sector interventions across Syria and is well-positioned to respond quickly to emergencies. With an established presence, trained emergency teams, and ongoing coordination with clusters and local authorities, IYD will ensure the delivery of timely, efficient, and accountable assistance within 48 hours of trigger activation. ltspangtIYD proposes the following activities: lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtMPCA response targeting 500 households in Aleppo and Idleb governorates. These households include newly displaced families and host community members affected by sudden displacement, escalations in conflict, or natural shocks (e.g., floods, windstorms, heavy rain, and snowstorms) in Northwest Syria. ltspangtBy providing USD 150 per household—as harmonized by the CWG—this intervention will immediately address basic survival needs such as food, water, medicines, hygiene items, and essentials, giving affected families the agency and flexibility to respond to their most pressing priorities. lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtTo address immediate food insecurity, 5,000 households will receive ready-to-eat rations (RTERs) within the first five days of displacement. This intervention will prevent negative coping mechanisms and support stabilization during the initial days of displacement.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe intervention also includes rapidly distributing 150 core NFI kits and 150 returnee kits and establishing safe spaces and service points along displacement routes. IYD will ensure community engagement and coordinate with local stakeholders to ensure context-appropriate implementation. All activities will adhere to SNFI and cluster standards 2025 guidelines and follow the core humanitarian principles. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtUnder the protection intervention, IYD aims to support affected populations in both Aleppo and Idleb through rapid and life-saving protection interventions. The project will establish and operate six reception centers to provide PFA and referrals for persons with specific protection needs. Mobile protection teams will be deployed to deliver community-based services, including awareness raising on GBV, PSEA, and protection risks. Safe transportation will be provided for at-risk individuals requiring urgent relocation or access to services. A dedicated protection hotline will be established to offer real-time information, remote PFA, and referrals. Legal awareness sessions and counseling will support individuals facing civil documentation. Child-focused non-structured PSS and recreational activities will be conducted to enhance children's psychosocial well-being. Awareness sessions and IEC material distribution will ensure communities are informed of their rights and available services. Targeted cash assistance will be provided to households at risk of eviction or forced relocation. The project ensures gender-sensitive, inclusive, and coordinated protection responses during emergencies.lt/pgt
